events.title: Lincoln Proclaims a National Thanksgiving
events.description: In the middle of the Civil War, President Abraham Lincoln issued a proclamation setting the last Thursday of November as a national day of Thanksgiving and praise.
events.significance: The proclamation helped establish Thanksgiving as an annual national holiday in the United States.

events.title: Iraq Joins the League of Nations as an Independent State
events.description: Iraq ended its status as a British mandate and was admitted to the League of Nations as a sovereign country.
events.significance: Iraq's independence is still marked as a national day, and it was a landmark in the end of the mandate system in the Middle East.

events.title: Britain Tests Its First Atomic Bomb
events.description: Operation Hurricane, a 25-kiloton nuclear device, was detonated off the Monte Bello Islands, Western Australia.
events.significance: The test made Britain the third nuclear-armed nation, after the United States and the Soviet Union.

events.title: Germany Reunites
events.description: East Germany formally joined the Federal Republic of Germany, ending 45 years of division. The change came less than a year after the fall of the Berlin Wall.
events.significance: Reunification closed a defining chapter of the Cold War and created Europe's most populous democracy.

events.title: O.J. Simpson Acquitted of Murder
events.description: After a widely televised trial in Los Angeles, a jury found O.J. Simpson not guilty of murdering Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman.
events.significance: The 'trial of the century' sparked national debate about race, celebrity and the justice system, and it changed how the media covers courtroom dramas.
